title: Braun SK 4 · Sender knob, replacement for printing

subject.summary: The large tuning knob of a Braun SK 4, modelled at its real 33 mm across and 19.6 mm high as a printable replacement: a skirted cone with twenty-four flutes, a raised indicator bar, and a 6.4 mm bore 14 mm deep with a flat for the shaft key.

sources.title: The owner's request
sources.ref: A printable replacement for the one missing large control knob of the owner's Braun SK 4; at real size, with body, grip, indicator line and a bored, flat-keyed shaft hole.

sources.title: Front view, lid closed (Alf van Beem, CC0)
sources.ref: refs/photo-1.jpg : the large tuning knob at the right of the deck, 3.02 px per mm on the front face.

sources.title: Deck close-up, lid open (With Associates, CC BY-SA 2.0)
sources.ref: refs/photo-2.jpg : the knob's taper, fluted side, top face and indicator bar.

sources.title: Braun SK 4 record
sources.ref: https://die-neue-sammlung.de/en/objekt/radio-phono-combination-stereo-phonosuper-sk4-1 : a 1956 set whose controls are light grey; the knob is one of them.

facts.value: Sender knob for the Braun Phonosuper SK 4

facts.note: 33 mm across the skirt, read off photo-1 against the 580 mm body: the large knob is about 1.5 times the 22 mm small knobs and clearly the largest control.
19.6 mm over the skirt: the knob stands about twice as tall as a small knob's 17 mm.

facts.value: A raised bar across the top face, running to the rim
facts.note: Both large and small knobs in the photographs carry a pointer.

facts.value: 6.4 mm bore, 14 mm deep, with a 0.8 mm flat
facts.note: DESIGNED, not measured: the owner will measure the shaft before printing. 6.4 mm suits a 6.0 mm shaft with running clearance; the flat 0.8 mm deep and 4.2 mm across suits a shaft with one flat.
The original is a moulded grey knob; this is a replacement, so it is designed to print (no overhangs, flat bottom, flutes coarse enough for a 0.4 mm nozzle).

parts.label: Skirt
parts.note: A 35 mm collar, 2.5 mm high, that stands on the panel and hides the nut; its diameter is read from photo-1, where the knob is about 1.5 times the 22 mm small knobs.

parts.label: Knob body
parts.note: A 33 mm cone tapering to 29.2 mm over 19.9 mm, with a 6.4 mm bore 14 mm deep: one revolved solid, closed at the bottom, so it prints without supports. Diameter, height and taper are traced off the photographs; the bore is designed to fit.

parts.label: Bore flat
parts.note: A 0.8 mm flat, 4.2 mm across, on the bore's wall: the SK 4's knobs are keyed on a shaft with one flat. DESIGNED to fit - measure the shaft across the flat before printing and change BORE_R and this depth to match.

parts.label: Grip flute
parts.note: Twenty-four shallow flutes, 0.5 mm proud, in a band 12.5 mm tall: the fine knurl visible on the knob's side in photo-2, coarse enough to print on a 0.4 mm nozzle.

parts.label: Indicator line
parts.note: A 2.2 x 10.5 mm bar raised 0.9 mm across the top face, running out to the rim: the pointer the photographs show on the large knob.

authoring.provenance_note: Sizes are of two kinds and each part says which: the skirt, body and indicator are traced off the photographs, the bore and its flat are designed to fit a shaft the owner will measure. Nothing here is a moulded original's measurement.

identity.feature: A 33 mm skirted cone, 19.6 mm high, the deck's largest control
Twenty-four shallow flutes round the grip
A raised indicator bar running to the rim
A bored, flat-keyed shaft hole (designed, not measured)

next: Measure the shaft across its flat and re-cut knob-bore-flat if the shaft is not a 6 mm D.
The original knob is light grey; print in a matching filament or paint it.
A 0.4 mm nozzle prints the 0.5 mm flutes cleanly; at 0.6 mm they will blur.
